messages:
maya: heads up — getting a spike in GPU preemptions in us-west-2. seen a bunch of evictions around 2026-03-05T22:13Z for pool gpu-reserved-2. trying to link to request traces but kibana is noisy. anyone seen this pattern before?

jonathan: do you have an example trace id or corr id? can you paste the exact kube event and the node name? might be kube-driven preemptions or a cloud patch job.

maya: grabbed one trace id from our inference logs: trace:3a9b12c4f9e. hit this simple kube event snippet from node logs: 

```
Mar 05 22:12:58 gpunode-118 kubelet[...]: Eviction manager: evicting pod "inference-worker-67". reason: Preemption
Mar 05 22:13:02 gpunode-118 systemd[1]: Starting reboot.target: Applied kernel update
```

maya: tried a quick kibana query but hit too many results. posted possible kql below.

jonathan: drop the full KQL and a loki example, i'll try joining with traces. small queries help.

jonathan: Kibana KQL (try limited time range and index):

```
index: infra-logs-* AND (event.dataset:kube.events OR message:Evict*) AND kubernetes.node.name:"gpunode-118" AND region:"us-west-2"
```

jonathan: Loki (Grafana Explore) quick filter:

```
{job="kube-logs", namespace="gpu-resources"} |= "Eviction" | json | trace_id="3a9b12c4f9e"
```

observability-bot: [ALERT] GPU_Preemption_Rate firing on us-west-2 (severity=critical) — rate > 0.2/sec across gpu-reserved-2 (fired=3m). alert link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/gpu-preempts?orgId=1

lina: also check the rollout/controller jobs around that time — we've had automated kernel patch jobs in that region before. look at infra-ops:patch-schedule label on nodes.

avi: can we correlate with our prefix/KV cache flush logs? if preemption showed during long-tail generation it could explain partial outputs. search in inference logs for trace:3a9b12c4f9e and kv_flush.

maya: ran a join: kibana returned ~8 eviction events matching that trace window across 3 nodes. loki trace lookup returned the same trace id inside the inference worker stderr: "received SIGTERM during kv_flush".

jonathan: that SIGTERM -> kernel update/auto-reboot fits. who owns patch-schedule for gpu-reserved-2? we should disable auto-patch for dedicated pools.

lina: infra-ops scheduled that maintenance window (ops-team). tagging @ops-leads. plan: pause autopatch for pools with reserved capacity and create a non-disruptive test window.

maya: quick TL;DR: correlated Kibana and Loki using trace id 3a9b12c4f9e, found SIGTERM on nodes and matching Prometheus alert. root cause appears to be scheduled kernel updates causing node drains/reboots.

jonathan: thanks — i'll open a follow-up runbook item to add a Grafana panel for preemptions by pool and a Kibana saved query for trace joins. also add a short alert suppression when we intentionally drain nodes.

maya: created issue: https://redwood.internal/ops/issue/4621 — will update after ops disables autopatch on gpu-reserved-2. :thumbsup:

avi: noted, also will add a quick query to the SLO dashboard to show token loss by preemption events.

maya: closing this thread once ops confirms. thanks all.
